translation_en: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, that ‘Abd Allah ibn Ka‘b ibn Malik, who used to lead Ka‘b, his father’s son, when he became blind, said: I heard Ka‘b ibn Malik tell the story of his staying behind from the expedition to Tabuk. Ka‘b said: I never stayed behind from an expedition the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, undertook except the expedition to Tabuk. I had also stayed behind from the expedition of Badr, but the Prophet did not reproach anyone who had stayed behind from it. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had set out intending to intercept the caravan of Quraysh, until Allah brought them together with their enemy unexpectedly. I had been present with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on the Night of al-‘Aqabah, when we pledged firmly to follow Islam. I would not trade being present there for being present at Badr, even though Badr is more widely remembered among people. My circumstances when I stayed behind from that expedition were that I had never been stronger or more prosperous. By Allah, before that I had never owned two riding camels at once, but I had both of them for that expedition. Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, intended an expedition, he would conceal his real destination by indicating another one. But when that expedition came, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, undertook it in intense heat, facing a long journey through desert and a numerous enemy. He made the destination clear to the Muslims so they could prepare properly for the expedition, and told them where he intended to go. The Muslims with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, were numerous, and they were not all listed in an official register. Ka‘b said: A man who wanted to stay behind would think that he could remain hidden unless Allah revealed something about him. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, set out on that expedition when the fruit was ripe and the shade was pleasant. The Messenger of Allah and the Muslims with him prepared themselves. I would go out in the morning intending to prepare with them, then return having done nothing. I would tell myself, ‘I can do it.’ This continued until the people became serious about the expedition. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and the Muslims with him set out, while I had done none of my preparations. I said, ‘I will prepare a day or two after they leave, then catch up with them.’ I went out the morning after they had departed to prepare, then returned having done nothing. I went out again, then returned having done nothing. This went on until they had hastened away and the expedition had passed me by. I considered setting out to catch them, and I wish I had done so, but it was not destined for me. After the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had departed, whenever I went out among the people, it grieved me that I saw no one there except a man suspected of hypocrisy or a man among the weak whom Allah had excused. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, did not mention me until he reached Tabuk. As he sat among the people in Tabuk, he asked, ‘What has happened to Ka‘b?’ A man from Banu Salimah said, ‘Messenger of Allah, his two fine garments and his admiration of himself have kept him back.’ Mu‘adh ibn Jabal said, ‘What a bad thing you have said! By Allah, Messenger of Allah, we know nothing about him except good.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said nothing. Ka‘b ibn Malik said: When I heard that he was returning, worry came over me. I began thinking of lies and asking myself what excuse I could use to escape his displeasure the next day. I sought advice from every sensible person in my family. But when I heard that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was close to arriving, falsehood left me. I knew that I could never get out of this by saying something false, so I resolved to tell the truth. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, arrived in the morning. When he returned from a journey, he would begin by going to the mosque, pray two units there, then sit down to meet the people. When he had done this, the men who had stayed behind came and began making excuses to him and swearing oaths. They were a little more than eighty men. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, accepted what they showed outwardly, accepted their pledges, and asked Allah to forgive them, leaving what was hidden in their hearts to Allah. I came to him. When I greeted him, he smiled with the smile of an angry man and said, ‘Come here.’ I walked over and sat before him. He said to me, ‘What kept you back? Had you not bought a riding camel?’ I said, ‘Yes. By Allah, if I were sitting before anyone else in this world, I would think that I could escape his displeasure with an excuse. I have been given the ability to argue persuasively. But by Allah, I know that if I tell you a lie today that pleases you, Allah will soon make you angry with me. If I tell you the truth, which will make you angry with me, I hope for Allah’s forgiveness. By Allah, I had no excuse. I had never been stronger or more prosperous than when I stayed behind.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘As for this man, he has told the truth. Get up and wait until Allah decides your case.’ I got up. Some men from Banu Salimah followed me and said, ‘By Allah, we never knew that you had committed a sin before this. You were unable to make an excuse to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, like the excuses the others who stayed behind made. The Messenger of Allah’s asking forgiveness for you would have been enough for your sin.’ By Allah, they kept reproaching me until I wanted to go back and contradict myself. Then I asked them, ‘Did anyone else meet the same response as I did?’ They said, ‘Yes. Two men said the same as you, and they were told what you were told.’ I asked, ‘Who are they?’ They said, ‘Murarah ibn al-Rabi‘ al-‘Amiri and Hilal ibn Umayyah al-Waqifi.’ They named two righteous men who had been present at Badr, examples for me to follow. I continued on after they named them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, forbade the Muslims to speak to the three of us, out of all those who had stayed behind. People avoided us and changed their attitude toward us, until the land itself seemed strange to me and no longer the land I knew. We remained in that state for fifty nights. My two companions gave in and stayed in their homes, weeping. I was the youngest and strongest of the group. I would go out, pray with the Muslims, and walk through the markets, but no one would speak to me. I would go to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, while he sat with people after prayer, greet him, and wonder to myself whether he had moved his lips to return my greeting. I would pray close to him and steal glances at him. When I turned toward my prayer, he would face me; when I turned toward him, he would turn away from me. When people’s coldness toward me had lasted a long time, I walked until I climbed over the wall into the garden of Abu Qatadah, my cousin and the person I loved most. I greeted him, but by Allah, he did not return my greeting. I said, ‘Abu Qatadah, I ask you by Allah: do you know that I love Allah and His Messenger?’ He remained silent. I asked him again, and he remained silent. I asked a third time, and he said, ‘Allah and His Messenger know best.’ My eyes overflowed with tears, and I turned away and climbed back over the wall. As I was walking through the market of Madinah, a Nabatean from among the people of Syria, who had brought food to sell in Madinah, began asking, ‘Who can direct me to Ka‘b ibn Malik?’ People started pointing him toward me. When he came to me, he handed me a letter from the king of Ghassan. It said: ‘To continue: I have heard that your companion has treated you harshly. Allah has not placed you in a land of humiliation and neglect. Come to us, and we will comfort you.’ When I read it, I said, ‘This too is a trial.’ I went with it to the oven and burned it. When forty of the fifty nights had passed, a messenger from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came to me and said, ‘The Messenger of Allah commands you to keep away from your wife.’ I asked, ‘Should I divorce her, or what should I do?’ He said, ‘No. Just stay apart from her and do not go near her.’ He sent the same message to my two companions. I said to my wife, ‘Go to your family and stay with them until Allah decides this matter.’ Ka‘b said: The wife of Hilal ibn Umayyah came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Hilal ibn Umayyah is an old, helpless man with no servant. Would you dislike it if I served him?’ He said, ‘No, but he must not come near you.’ She said, ‘By Allah, he has no desire or strength for anything. By Allah, he has done nothing but weep from the day his case began until this day.’ Someone from my family said to me, ‘Why don’t you ask the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, for permission concerning your wife, as he gave Hilal ibn Umayyah’s wife permission to serve him?’ I said, ‘By Allah, I will not ask the Messenger of Allah for permission about her. How do I know what the Messenger of Allah would say if I asked him about her, when I am a young man?’ I remained in that state for ten more nights, completing fifty nights since the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had forbidden people to speak to us. When I had prayed the dawn prayer on the morning of the fiftieth night, I was on the roof of one of our houses. I sat in the state Allah had described: my soul had become constricted, and the earth, vast as it was, had become constricted for me. I heard the voice of someone calling from the top of Mount Sal‘, shouting at the top of his voice, ‘Ka‘b ibn Malik, rejoice!’ I fell down in prostration, knowing that relief had come. After the dawn prayer, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, announced that Allah had accepted our repentance. People went to bring us the good news. Some went to my two companions. A man rode a horse toward me, and another man from Aslam ran up the mountain to call me. The voice was faster than the horse. When the man whose voice I had heard came to bring me the good news, I took off my two garments and gave them to him for his good news. By Allah, I owned nothing else that day. I borrowed two garments and put them on, then set out for the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. People came to meet me in groups, congratulating me on my repentance and saying, ‘May Allah’s acceptance of your repentance bring you joy.’ Ka‘b said: I entered the mosque and found the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sitting with people around him. Talhah ibn ‘Ubayd Allah got up and hurried toward me, shook my hand, and congratulated me. By Allah, no other man from the Emigrants got up for me, and I will never forget that kindness from Talhah. When I greeted the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his face shining with joy, he said, ‘Rejoice in the best day that has passed over you since your mother gave birth to you.’ I asked, ‘Is this from you, Messenger of Allah, or from Allah?’ He said, ‘No, rather it is from Allah.’ When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was happy, his face would shine until it looked like a piece of the moon, and we could recognize that in him. When I sat before him, I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, as part of my repentance I will give up some of my wealth as charity to Allah and His Messenger.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Keep some of your wealth; that will be better for you.’ I said, ‘Then I will keep my share at Khaybar.’ I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Allah saved me only because I told the truth. Part of my repentance is that for the rest of my life I will speak only the truth.’ By Allah, I know of no Muslim whom Allah has tested with truthful speech since I told that to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, more favorably than He tested me. From the time I said that to the Messenger of Allah until this day, I have never deliberately told a lie, and I hope that Allah will protect me for the rest of my life. Allah revealed to His Messenger, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, ‘Allah has turned in mercy to the Prophet and the Emigrants…’ through the words ‘and be with the truthful’ (9:117–119). By Allah, after Allah guided me to Islam, He has never granted me a blessing greater in my eyes than my having told the truth to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and not lied to him and perished as those who lied perished. When Allah sent down revelation about those who lied, He said the worst thing He said about anyone. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said, ‘They will swear by Allah to you when you return…’ through the words ‘Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people’ (9:95–96). Ka‘b said: We three had stayed behind, unlike those whose excuses and oaths the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, accepted. He accepted their pledges, asked Allah to forgive them, and left their hidden matters to Allah. He deferred our case until Allah decided it. That is why Allah said, ‘And [He also turned in mercy] to the three who were left behind’ (9:118). What Allah meant was not that we had been left behind from the expedition. Rather, He left our cases pending and deferred them apart from those who had sworn to him and made excuses that he accepted.
